known_limitations: REINDEX REQUIRED: chunk bodies and spans both change, so any index built before this commit carries comment and marker text in its bodies and blank-padded spans. Nothing here rebuilds an existing database.

The readable-signal gate is still ASCII-only (r'[^A-Za-z0-9]+' with a 20-character floor), so a note whose prose is entirely non-Latin collapses to the title-only fallback chunk and is never indexed. This bounds how far the D2 unicode widening can reach; the widening is observable only for a non-Latin word sitting beside enough ASCII prose. Pre-existing and unchanged.

fold_text coerces a non-string argument with str(), turning None into 'none'. Not reachable today (schema columns are NOT NULL and every caller passes text), but it would convert a type error into a silent token.
D1's comment and marker stripping replaces each match with a single space, so a body can retain a lone space between blank lines. Cosmetic.

D3 is a user-visible policy change: questions made only of stopwords and meta-words now return the no-evidence response. Agent C found no question that retrieved useful evidence on the base and fails now; the two that returned anything returned LOW-strength noise. Codex is right that this is nonetheless a real recall tradeoff, and the earlier claim that no plausible useful case exists was too strong: 'what did I say?' is all stopwords and meta-words, and in a journal or transcript vault that could be a legitimate request. Reversible by restoring the fallback.
F2 remains open: phrase_bonus, all_terms_bonus, gentle loosening of the 0.30 coverage floor, the execute_match candidate limit and the fts_token prefix threshold are unpinned.
Verified against synthetic fixtures with ollama_chat stubbed; no model, database of the owner's, or vault was exercised.

One vacuous assertion remains, at tests/test_retrieval_core_e2e.py:439: inside the coverage-boundary loop, all(r['term_coverage'] >= 0.30 for r in got) is vacuously true on the iteration whose expected row count is 0. The len(got) == expected check above it carries that row's real content, and the other two iterations exercise the predicate substantively.

Four surviving mutants are test gaps, not defects; the shipped code is correct in each case. The one worth a fixture is a greedy comment stripper (<!--.*-->  rather than non-greedy), which would delete prose BETWEEN two HTML comments - the same destructive family as the fence regression, on the one D1 literal the fixtures already covered. No fixture has two comments or a multi-line comment. Also unpinned: fence indent tolerance, the {3,} blank-run threshold at its boundary, and the [ \t]+ horizontal-whitespace collapse (a fifth cleanup literal this package did not claim).
Tilde (~~~) fences and lines of four or more backticks are not recognised as fences, so their markers are retained. Nothing is deleted. Pre-existing scope, not changed here.
CRLF is unreachable in the real path: Path.read_text uses universal-newline decoding, so \r\n becomes \n before chunk_note sees it.

Fence markers are removed from the evidence a note contributes, so a fenced block reaches the model as ordinary prose. Codex notes this removes a structural cue that attacker-controlled text was quoted rather than asserted. The system prompt still declares all evidence untrusted, so no trust boundary changes, but the cue is gone. Keeping the markers would be a design change beyond this defect and is left for an owner decision.

escalation.root_cause: Three attempts at D1 failed in the same direction: each fixed the pattern in front of me rather than the structure behind it. Markup cleanup is being done on a text buffer whose boundaries were already decided by a chunker that knows nothing about markup, so no amount of regex care inside flush() can protect a fenced block the chunker has already cut in half. D2 has the mirror problem: the reranker re-derives which terms matched by folding strings itself, instead of asking the index what it actually matched, so any fold that is not bit-exact with unicode61 diverges somewhere.
recommended_next: Split the package. D3 and D4 are finished and independently valuable; they could be re-cut as a small package with no D1 or D2 content and go through the gates cleanly.

D1 done properly needs fence state tracked in chunk_note's main loop, so a fenced block is never split across chunks and never reclassified. That is a chunking design change and belongs in its own approved package with a re-index.

D2 done properly probably means the reranker stops re-deriving matched terms by string comparison and instead takes them from what FTS5 returned. That removes the need for fold_text to agree with unicode61 at all, and is a larger change than a defect repair.

Until then D1 and D2 remain open defects in the merged base, unchanged from before this package: comments are not stripped and accented content is unreachable. Neither got worse on uep/work, because nothing was merged.
